metadata.case_name: SIU LEONG CHING v. PROFESSIONAL SCAFFOLDING ENGINEERING CO LTD AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_after: receptionist at a karaoke lounge in Shenzen

injuries.description: fracture of left inferior pubic rami (front pelvic bone)
source: fracture of left inferior pubic rami (front pelvic bone);
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pubis without disruption of pelvic ring

injuries.description: fracture of trochanter of right femur (the upper part of the thigh bone)
source: fracture of trochanter of right femur (the upper part of the thigh bone);
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of trochanteric section of femur

injuries.description: fracture of right talus (bone in hind foot)
source: fracture of right talus (bone in hind foot);

manifestations.description: stiffness of the right hip joint
right patello-femoral joint tenderness with crepitation
limited movements of the right hip joint
right knee joint movement and both ankle joint movements limited
decreased motor power in the right leg
X-ray had showed secondary osteoarthritis in the right ankle joint
cannot walk fast due to right hip and right ankle discomfort
walking tolerance is limited to 30 minutes
cannot undergo his sporting activities as swimming, hiking, cycling, and bowling
requires the help of railings when going up or down stairs

treatments_received: 27 May 2000: fixation of the hip fracture
5 June 2000: fixation of the calcaneus, fixation of the fibula and fusion of right subtalar joint
26 June 2000: closure of the ankle wound
24 November 2000: revision fixation of the hip fracture
9 January 2001: right ankle arthroscopy for the open release of the right ankle and foot
transfer to the Maclehose Medical Rehabilitation Centre on 27 June 2000 for rehabilitation and therapies
readmitted to Queen Mary Hospital on five occasions for orthopaedic treatments
treatments_future: possible future fusion of the right ankle joint when pain becomes unbearable

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: unable to take part in many of the sporting activities which he had enjoyed before the accident.
cannot walk fast due to right hip and right ankle discomfort; walking tolerance is limited to 30 minutes; requires the help of railings when going up or down stairs; unable to squat down.
could not return to his pre-accident work as a scaffolder but would be restricted to sedentary jobs.
